For the present we define that to be self-sufficient, which taken alone makes life choice, worthy
and to be in one of nothing, now of such kind we think happiness to be, and further to be
most choice, worthy of all things, not being reckoned with any other thing, for if it were
so reckoned, it is plain we must then allow it, with the addition of ever so small a good
to be more choice, worthy than it was before, because what is put to it becomes an addition
of so much more good, and of goods the greater is ever the more choice, worthy.

thought to belong to the final good.

for man is by nature adapted to a social existence.
